system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Re:** Seller's "Key Negotiated Positions" and Disclosure Letter dated 22 September 2026
**Status:** Privileged – prepared for the Buyer

---

## 0. Preliminary point – how the Seller's package tries to frame this review

Before the substance, three framing devices in the Seller's cover note should be rejected outright:

1. **The "[STANDARD] / FINAL / do not re-open" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note".** These are the other side's labels, not ours. Nothing marked [STANDARD] has been "cleared by both sides" as far as our records show, and the note that the review "may proceed on the basis" that the limitation and disclosure package is accepted is simply an attempt to have us waive the most valuable points in the deal. I have reviewed every clause on its merits and treated all of them as open. **Action:** please confirm with our principals whether *any* of these points were in fact agreed at principal level; if not, our mark-up should say so expressly in the cover note.
2. **The "market context" preamble.** It is a selective statement. Caps of 10–20% and ~1% baskets do occur in SaaS deals, but (a) they apply to *general* warranties only, never to title/capacity, tax or specific indemnities, and (b) a *constructive* buyer-knowledge qualification ("discoverable from the data room") is not market. The preamble should be given no weight.
3. **The disclosure letter is dated 22 September 2026; today is 5 November 2026.** Six weeks have passed on a deal with an open privacy incident, an un-repaid lender with change-of-control rights and an unobtained key-customer consent. Every disclosure is stale. We need a bring-down disclosure letter at signing and at Completion, and the Seller's position on each of the items below needs to be re-stated as at today.

Also note: **the disclosure letter skips from [1.2] to [1.4]**. Ask what [1.3] said and why it was removed.

---

## 1. Limitation of liability package (cl 12, 13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

### 1.1 General cap – 20% (AUD 4.8m)
Within the range we might ultimately accept for general warranties, *but only if* the carve-outs below are agreed and we have adequate covenant support (see §1.6). Opening position: 30–50%; land at 20–25% only as a trade for the carve-outs.

### 1.2 Fundamental / title / capacity warranties under the same cap – **reject**
The Seller's proposal to cap title and capacity warranties at 20% "for administrative simplicity" is off-market and commercially unacceptable. If we do not get good title to 100% of the shares we have paid AUD 24m for AUD 4.8m of recourse. Title, capacity, authority, no-encumbrance and share-capital warranties must be capped at **100% of price** (plus costs), with a limitation period of **not less than 6 years** (or the statutory period for a deed – 12 years in NSW if the SPA is executed as a deed, which we should require).

### 1.3 Tax – **separate regime required**
"Settled under the general regime" means tax warranties die at 18 months and sit inside AUD 4.8m. The ATO's standard amendment period is 4 years (unlimited for fraud/evasion). We need: a stand-alone **tax indemnity** (pre-Completion tax, on a dollar-for-dollar basis, no disclosure qualification), **7-year** claims period, cap at 100% of price (or at minimum a materially higher separate cap).

### 1.4 De minimis AUD 25k / basket AUD 250k / deductible structure
- De minimis ~0.1% is tolerable; push to AUD 10–15k.
- Basket at ~1.04% is at the upper edge of market; push to 0.5%.
- **"Only the excess above the basket is recoverable" = a deductible, not a tipping basket.** Buyer position: tipping (once the basket is exceeded, recover from the first dollar).
- None of the thresholds should apply to fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, leakage or Completion obligations.

### 1.5 Time limits and the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" default
- 18 months for general warranties is short for a SaaS business whose first full post-Completion audit will not be complete by then. Push for **24 months** (minimum: 18 months plus 60 days after signing of the first post-Completion audited accounts).
- The proposed default that **every** limitation applies to **every** Claim unless we have carved it out reverses the usual drafting and is a trap: anything we fail to list is caught. Flip the default – limitations in cl 12 apply only to general Warranty Claims; everything else (fundamental, tax, indemnities, leakage, Completion covenants, restraints, fraud) is outside unless expressly brought in.

### 1.6 Exclusive remedy / non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)
Must carve out: fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment; the specific indemnities; claims under the Completion mechanics (price adjustment/leakage); breach of pre-Completion covenants; and our statutory rights (an attempt to exclude liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under the ACL is of doubtful efficacy in any event, and a court will not enforce a non-reliance clause against fraud). Non-reliance should be limited to statements *outside* the SPA, not to the warranties themselves.

### 1.7 Covenant strength – a point the Seller's package is silent on
The Seller is **Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd**, a venture vehicle that will presumably distribute proceeds to its investors shortly after Completion. A 20% cap is worthless against an empty shell. We need one or more of: **escrow/retention** (I would suggest 10–15% for 24 months, with a separate longer-dated tranche against the specific indemnities), a **parent/fund guarantee**, or **W&I insurance** (with the Seller bearing a meaningful retention). This should be raised now, because it interacts with every number in §1.

---

## 2. Disclosure and Buyer knowledge (Sch 7, Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2], cl 8.3) – **the single most important push-back**

### 2.1 General disclosure of the entire data room and "publicly searchable corporate records"
Under the Seller's draft, *every* fact in DD-002 to DD-012 and every public register is deemed disclosed against *every* warranty. Combined with the disclosure letter's refusal to characterise anything (para 11 and [1.4]), the warranties become close to meaningless – the Seller can say the breach was "in the data room".

Buyer position:
- Delete general data-room disclosure. Disclosure only via the Disclosure Letter, and only to the extent **"fairly disclosed"** – defined as disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely financial impact.
- No disclosure against fundamental warranties, the tax indemnity or the specific indemnities.
- No disclosure of "publicly searchable records" at all (or at most specific ASIC/PPSR searches we actually conducted on a named date).

### 2.2 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge including "discoverable" matters and advisers' knowledge – **reject entirely**
This is a constructive-knowledge exclusion. Everything in §§3–9 below is in the data room, so under cl 8.3 we would have *no claim* on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the bonuses, the privacy incident or the renewals, even though the Seller's own letter admits none of them is resolved. It also imports our lawyers' and accountants' knowledge.

Buyer position: delete. If a knowledge qualifier is the price of something we want more, limit it to the **actual** knowledge of two or three named Wattlebridge individuals, derived solely from the Disclosure Letter, and exclude the specific indemnities, fundamental warranties and tax in any event. Add a statement that the Buyer's DD does not limit or qualify the warranties.

### 2.3 Disclosure Letter [1.4] and para 11
Acceptable as boilerplate *only* if the specific indemnities below do not depend on the Seller admitting anything. Note the Seller has carefully disclosed facts but denied every conclusion – that is precisely why the items below must be dealt with by indemnity and Completion mechanics, not warranty.

---

## 3. Bluefen consent (~30% of revenue) – cl 3 / 6.3

The Seller's note says the consent "is addressed". The Seller's own disclosure (para 2) says there is **no final written consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied**. Those statements are inconsistent and the cover note should not be relied on.

Buyer position:
- **Condition precedent** to Completion (not a post-Completion covenant): written, unconditional consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2, in a form approved by the Buyer, **together with** evidence that each cl 11.3 condition is satisfied or waived. "Treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" is not acceptable if the consent is conditional.
- Seller to use **all reasonable endeavours** (not "reasonable endeavours"), with an information covenant and Buyer participation in discussions.
- Specific warranty that Bluefen has not indicated any intention to terminate, re-price or reduce volumes, and a bring-down at Completion.
- Fallback if the Seller resists a hard CP: price retention/escrow sized to the revenue at risk, plus a termination right.

---

## 4. Riverlark Bank facility (~AUD 3.2m) – cl 2 / 7

The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A release "to be provided following Completion" is inconsistent with that and with DD-003 cl 8.1 (change of control): on Completion the Company would be in default to its lender with security still on foot. We would be buying a company with AUD 3.2m of defaulted debt and relying on the Seller to fix it afterwards.

Buyer position:
- Facility repaid **at Completion out of the purchase price** via the funds flow (payout letter from Riverlark delivered pre-Completion, deed of release and discharge of all security, PPSR discharges and any share-mortgage release delivered **at Completion** as Completion deliverables).
- The AUD 3.2m (plus break costs, accrued interest and fees to the Completion date) is deducted from the price.
- Confirm whether Riverlark holds security over the **shares** (likely in a VC-backed company). If so, title cannot pass free of encumbrance without the release – which links to the title point in §10.

---

## 5. Completion bonuses (AUD 420,000) – DD-005 / funds flow

The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" yet does not include them in the funds flow. They are triggered by Completion and (per the continued-employment condition) will be *paid by the Company after Completion* – i.e. by us.

Buyer position:
- Treat as a **Transaction Cost / debt-like item**: deduct from the price the gross amount **plus on-costs** (12% superannuation, NSW payroll tax ~5.45%, any leave accruals) – roughly AUD 490–500k, subject to our tax advisers' figure.
- Alternatively, Seller funds them through the funds flow at Completion, with a specific indemnity for any shortfall and for any claim by an employee whose bonus is withheld.
- Ask for the bonus letters and confirm no other change-of-control payments (options, accelerated vesting, retention) exist.

---

## 6. Ironquay Development Studio IP – cl 11.1

DD-004 cl 7.3: SOW3 Project Materials do **not** transfer until every SOW3 fee is paid. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; there is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment. On the current record, the Company **does not own** the SOW3 deliverables. For a SaaS business that is a core-asset issue, not a payables issue. An indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" covers the AUD 180k invoice and nothing else – not an injunction, re-development costs, a customer claim, or Ironquay's licence to the material.

Buyer position:
- **Completion deliverables:** evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a **confirmatory deed of assignment** of all SOW3 IP from Ironquay to the Company (plus moral-rights consents from Ironquay personnel). If unpaid at Completion, the AUD 180k is deducted from the price and paid through the funds flow.
- Specific indemnity for **all Loss** arising from any defect in the Company's title to, or any third-party claim in respect of, the Ironquay deliverables – uncapped or at a separate cap, no basket, 6-year period.
- Full IP warranties (ownership of all platform IP, no third-party development without assignment, open-source compliance) outside the general-disclosure regime.

---

## 7. Export / privacy incident – DD-006, cl 4.6 / Sch 6

The Seller calls this "preliminary operational… not expected to be material". It is a download link containing ~1,240 individuals' personal information sent to an unintended external recipient. Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme in the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth), the Company had to assess within **30 days** whether the breach is likely to result in serious harm and notify the OAIC and affected individuals if so. The incident predates 22 September; it is now 5 November. Either the assessment has been completed (and we have not been told the outcome) or the Company is already outside the statutory window. Penalties for serious interferences with privacy now run to the greater of AUD 50m, 3× benefit or 30% of adjusted turnover, and the records likely include Bluefen's and other customers' personnel, triggering contractual notification duties.

Buyer position:
- Pre-signing: full incident report, log evidence of whether the link was accessed, the NDB assessment, and all customer/regulator correspondence.
- Completion covenant: investigation concluded, notifications (if required) made, and remediation steps agreed with the Buyer before Completion.
- **Specific indemnity** for all Loss (regulatory penalties, notification costs, customer claims, credits, remediation, legal costs) arising from the DD-006 incident and any related incident – outside the general cap and basket, no disclosure qualification, minimum 6 years.
- Data-protection and cybersecurity warranties with a bring-down at Completion; MAC clause to expressly capture regulatory action.

---

## 8. Sandbar supplier renewals (3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000) – DD-008 / DD-011

Three identical renewals, disclosed separately but to be "read together", and the Seller "does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course". Splitting a single AUD 330k commitment into three AUD 110k contracts may be innocent, but it is also how commitments are kept below approval or materiality thresholds. Questions: were they signed in the Locked Box/pre-Completion period? Are they prepaid, accrued or future liabilities? Are they terminable for convenience? Are they needed to run the platform?

Buyer position: obtain the three contracts; if committed but not yet accrued/paid, treat as a working-capital or debt-like adjustment in the completion accounts (or as Leakage if locked box); warranty that there are no other related or split commitments; pre-Completion covenant requiring Buyer consent for new commitments above a threshold applied on an **aggregated** basis.

---

## 9. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)

- **Lease:** the Seller frames it as a "notification obligation" only. Confirm by reading the clause ourselves. If it is notification only, make giving the notice (and landlord acknowledgment) a pre-Completion step so there is no post-Completion dispute. If it is a change-of-control consent, add to CPs.
- **Mossvale:** the Seller says the assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale. That depends on whether "assignment" or "change of control" is defined to include a change in shareholding – a very common drafting point. Review DD-009 ourselves; if there is any ambiguity, obtain a comfort letter/consent from Mossvale pre-Completion rather than rely on the Seller's reading. Warranty that no customer or supplier contract contains a change-of-control right other than those listed.

---

## 10. Title to the shares – DD-012

The Seller relies solely on the Company's own share register and expressly notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification. The register is maintained by the Company (i.e. the Seller's nominees). We should independently verify: current ASIC company extract; the constitution (pre-emptive rights, drag/tag, board approval to transfer); any shareholders' agreement; options, SAFEs, convertible notes or warrants (common in a VC-backed company); PPSR search for security over the shares (Riverlark – see §4); and the chain of transfers into Harbourglass. Title warranties uncapped (§1.2), and Completion deliverables to include resignations, share transfer, updated register, and release of any share security.

---

## 11. Funds flow and price mechanics

The Seller says the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics" but has not provided it, and its own disclosure letter confirms it omits the bonuses and the Riverlark repayment. We cannot sign off a funds flow we have not seen. Request it now and ensure it shows: Riverlark payout; Ironquay AUD 180k (if unpaid); bonuses plus on-costs; any Sandbar accrued amounts; Seller transaction costs; escrow deposit. Confirm whether the mechanism is completion accounts or locked box – if locked box, we need a Leakage indemnity (dollar-for-dollar, outside the cap) and the bonuses/renewals must be expressly Leakage unless Permitted.

---

## 12. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer position / action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Framing | "[STANDARD]/FINAL", stale 22 Sep letter | Reject labels; confirm with principals nothing is agreed; bring-down disclosure at signing and Completion; ask about missing para [1.3] |
| 1 | General cap | 20% | Open 30–50%; accept ~20–25% only with carve-outs and covenant support |
| 2 | Title/capacity | Same cap and 18 months | 100% of price; ≥6 years; execute SPA as a deed |
| 3 | Tax | General regime | Separate tax indemnity; 7 years; 100% cap |
| 4 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k deductible | 10–15k / 0.5% tipping; not applicable to fundamental, tax, indemnities |
| 5 | Time limit / default | 18 months; limits apply to all Claims | 24 months; limits apply only to general warranties |
| 6 | Exclusive remedy / non-reliance | All Claims | Carve out fraud, indemnities, Completion mechanics, covenants, statutory rights |
| 7 | Covenant strength | Silent | Escrow 10–15% / guarantee / W&I |
| 8 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public records | Disclosure Letter only; "fairly disclosed"; none against fundamental/tax/indemnities |
| 9 | Buyer knowledge cl 8.3 | Actual + constructive + advisers | Delete (fallback: actual knowledge of named individuals, via Disclosure Letter only) |
| 10 | Bluefen (30% revenue) | "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours | Hard CP: unconditional consent + cl 11.3 conditions satisfied; all reasonable endeavours; retention fallback |
| 11 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Release post-Completion | Repay at Completion via funds flow; payout letter, deed of release, PPSR discharge as Completion deliverables; price deduction |
| 12 | Bonuses AUD 420k | Not in funds flow | Deduct gross + super + payroll tax (~AUD 490–500k) or Seller funds at Completion; indemnity |
| 13 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to AUD 180k | Payment + confirmatory IP assignment at Completion; broad specific indemnity outside cap; full IP warranties |
| 14 | DD-006 privacy incident | "Not material" | Full incident file; NDB assessment status; investigation closed pre-Completion; specific uncapped indemnity; data warranties |
| 15 | Sandbar 3 × 110k | Ordinary course | Obtain contracts; treat as working-capital/Leakage adjustment; aggregated consent threshold |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | No consent needed | Read clauses ourselves; notice/comfort letter pre-Completion; CoC warranty |
| 17 | Title | Share register only | Independent ASIC, constitution, SHA, PPSR, convertibles review; uncapped title warranties |
| 18 | Funds flow | Not provided | Request; must reflect items 11–13 and 15; confirm locked box vs completion accounts; Leakage indemnity |

**Priority order for the mark-up:** (1) delete cl 8.3 and general data-room disclosure; (2) Riverlark repaid at Completion; (3) Bluefen as a hard CP; (4) carve-outs from the cap/time limits for fundamental, tax and the specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Leakage); (5) escrow/guarantee; (6) the numerical thresholds last – they are the cheapest concession for us to give once the structure is right.

Please let me know if you would like me to prepare the formal mark-up of the SPA clauses and a response Disclosure Letter commentary on the basis above, or a shorter negotiation note for the principals' call.
=== END ADVICE ===
